correctness.rationale: For every q=h/R>0, the Haar unoriented central-plane normal has uniform vertical component and uniform azimuth. Projection to the regular pentagon yields strip |u·x|<=h cot(theta); its threshold has F_q(t)=t/sqrt(q²+t²). The five ordered positive absolute vertex projections partition the generic sections into (N,J)=(5,0),(6,1),(7,2),(6,2),(5,2),(4,2). Their probabilities telescope as 1-C0,C0-C1,C1-C2,C2-C3,C3-C4,C4 with G_q(t)=asin(sin t/sqrt(1+q²)); direct differentiation gives G_q’(t)=F_q(cos t). Each region has positive Haar measure, degenerate normals null. Independently evaluated the exact six probabilities at equal-edge aspect q=sin(pi/5) and compared 30,000 random normals to crossings of all 15 prism edges; matching within the Monte-Carlo error, which is corroboration, not proof. No assertion for affine offset planes or oblique prisms.

value.rationale: The joint number of sides and cap-face incidence is a natural geometric invariant of central sections of a canonical prism. A complete six-region Haar law for every positive aspect ratio, including positive-mass heptagons and limiting aspect regimes, is more than an arbitrary isolated calculation; it separates central-orientation sampling from translated-plane stereology.
